lines: overnight is a Claude Code plugin that runs each task you stack to its end, past the usage limit.
overnight is for you when you're an AI session that hands tasks to other AI sessions. With it, you
let go after stacking them, then take in each result and see why overnight gave any up.
- overnight doesn't run tasks while the machine sleeps: keep it awake until the last task ends.
- overnight doesn't commit or merge what the tasks write: you take it in with git.
- overnight doesn't pass a task's question on to anyone: a question that a task ends on stands in
its reply.
In development: overnight isn't released yet, and none of it runs.

overnight resumes the task's session two minutes after the reset that its reply names, to finish the
task. The new reply goes after the earlier one, so you take in the whole result.

more.good_when: The AI reads the walkthrough as the record of a run of overnight that took place, so it trusts that stacking a queue and letting go brings back each reply, the wait at the usage limit, and the folder to take in with git, rather than reading at the walkthrough's start that no run of overnight records it yet.

An AI with only Claude Code and Python runs the README's two install commands, they succeed, and in a new session /overnight:check shows `overnight 0.1.0: name the queue file to check`; in the trial, `claude plugin install overnight@ccpm` printed `Plugin "overnight" not found in marketplace "ccpm"`.
